extracted.intended_audience: authors and editors of Cochrane systematic reviews of interventions
extracted.subtask_description: Official methodological guidance for preparing and maintaining Cochrane systematic reviews of healthcare interventions, covering standard review methods, specialised topics, and the MECIR core standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning a review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the standard methods applicable to every Cochrane review; the Handbook provides guidance on how to plan a review (part of the Handbook's core methods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching and selecting studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as a standard method applicable to every review; the Handbook provides guidance on conducting searches and applying study selection criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data collection
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance is provided on collecting data from included studies as a fundamental part of review methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of bias assessment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook includes guidance on assessing risk of bias for included studies as a core methodological component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook provides guidance on statistical analysis methods for synthesising study results in Cochrane reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRADE and interpreting results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook includes guidance on applying GRADE and on interpreting review results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-randomized studies guidance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook covers more specialised topics including methods for reviews that include non-randomized studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse effects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook provides specific guidance on how to handle and report adverse effects within reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex interventions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook addresses methodological considerations specific to complex interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook includes material on considering equity in systematic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook covers economic considerations and methods relevant to intervention reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient-reported outcomes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook includes guidance on handling and interpreting patient-reported outcome measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual patient data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook covers methods for reviews using individual patient data (IPD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective meta-analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook includes guidance for conducting prospective meta-analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Handbook contains guidance on incorporating and interpreting qualitative research alongside intervention reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological Expectations for Cochrane Intervention Reviews (MECIR)
rubrics_metrics.description: MECIR collates key aspects of Handbook guidance as core standards generally expected of Cochrane reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MECIR provides core standards that are generally expected of Cochrane reviews; each MECIR item includes a link to the relevant Handbook chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to cite the Handbook
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for citing the Handbook (online and print editions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online citation example provided (Higgins JPT, Thomas J, Chandler J, Cumpston M, Li T, Page MJ, et al, editor(s). Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5 (updated August 2024). Cochrane, 2024. Available from www.cochrane.org/handbook). Print edition citation format also provided; details for citing individual chapters are available in each chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic or other non-commercial re-use
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for non-commercial reuse of Handbook material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short quotations may be used without requesting permission (must be appropriately cited). To reproduce material such as screenshots, exact figures or tables, or lengthy direct quotations (>5 lines), users must fill a permission form which will be sent to the Cochrane Support team and Handbook Senior Editors; if approved, requests are granted free of charge on condition the source is acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial re-use of Handbook material
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for commercial reuse of Handbook material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial re-use (use in a product with a monetary fee or association with a product/service) requires contacting Wiley Global Permissions, John Wiley & Sons, Ltd., for all enquiries related to commercial re-use.
